budget_items.topic: Budget preparation process and staff involvement
budget_items.what_was_said: Candidate described sitting on every budget subcommittee meeting in her current district and involving staff from the classroom level up in budget recommendations. No dollar figures were given.
Candidate said capital expenses, unlike the regular operating budget, should be projected further out to schedule roofing, building and curriculum-review cycles.
A member asked whether a public-facing, manipulable budget could be ready for the launch of the next school year; the candidate said yes, with frantic summer work.

Candidate described grants she oversees being approved, then unapproved, then approved again amid federal changes including the discussed dismantling of a cabinet department of education. No figures were cited.

budget_items.topic: Budget 'nice to haves' vs 'need to haves'
budget_items.what_was_said: Candidate described a decision framework asking what a program's impact and cost were and pushing for data before keeping or cutting it, without citing any figures.
A member described expensive, low-enrollment courses like honors anatomy that create scheduling costs; the candidate offered creative scheduling and combined-level teaching as responses.

budget_items.topic: Hiring staff who fill multiple roles
budget_items.what_was_said: Discussion of hiring practices intended to find teachers who can also coach or run extracurriculars, addressing budget pressure to have staff cover multiple needs. No figures were given.

decisions.decision: The chair reminded community members they may submit feedback on the candidate via survey, either online or in person.
The committee set the next day for deliberations on the finalist candidate.

minutes.headline: Committee interviewed superintendent finalist Joanie Manard for 75 minutes; no hiring vote, deliberations set for next day
minutes.summary: This special meeting was a 75-minute, 13-question interview of Joanie Manard, the finalist candidate for superintendent of schools, covering her background, budgeting philosophy, leadership style, student safety approach, staffing and hiring practices, and community relationships. No vote was taken on the candidacy itself; the committee adjourned by roll-call vote and set deliberations for the following day, and reminded the community it could submit feedback via survey.

what_happened.line: The School Committee held a 75-minute, 13-question interview with superintendent finalist Joanie Manard.
The candidate said a public-facing, editable budget tool could be ready by the next school year, with intensive summer work.
She described federal grant approvals being granted, withdrawn, and reinstated amid discussion of dismantling a federal education department.
No vote was taken on the candidacy; the committee adjourned by roll call and scheduled deliberations for the following day.

why_it_matters: The next superintendent sets budgeting process, staffing decisions, and the district's approach to programs like low-enrollment courses that residents fund through the school budget.
A promised public budget tool, if built, would change how residents can review school spending themselves.
Federal grant instability described in the interview could affect which programs the district can count on outside funding for.
